{{legend0|#92C5DE|Democratic hold}} {{legend0|#0671B0 |Democratic gain}} {{col-begin}} {{col-2}} '''Republican''' {{legend|#e27f90|50–60%}} {{legend|#CC2F4A|60–70%}} {{legend|#D40000|70–80%}} {{legend|#aa0000|80–90%}} {{legend|#800000|90–100%}} {{col-2}} '''Democratic''' {{legend|#86b6f2|50–60%}} {{legend|#4389E3|60–70%}} {{legend|#1666cb|70–80%}} {{legend|#0645b4|80–90%}} {{col-end}} }} {{ElectionsLA}} The '''2024 United States House of Representatives elections in Louisiana''' were held on November 5, 2024, to elect the six [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representatives]] from the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Louisiana]], one from each of the state's [[Louisiana's congressional districts|congressional districts]]. The elections coincided with the [[2024 United States presidential election|U.S. presidential election]], as well as [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2024 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various [[2024 United States elections|state and local elections]]. {{toclimit|2}} ==Overview== {{bar box|title=Popular vote|titlebar=#ddd|width=600px|barwidth=410px|bars={{bar percent|'''Republican'''|{{party color|Republican Party (United States)}}|65.49}} {{bar percent|Democratic|{{party color|Democratic Party (United States)}}|34.15}} {{bar percent|Other|#777777|0.36}}}}{{bar box|title=House seats|titlebar=#ddd|width=600px|barwidth=410px|bars={{bar percent|'''Republican'''|{{party color|Republican Party (United States)}}|66.67}} {{bar percent|Democratic|{{party color|Democratic Party (United States)}}|33.33}}}} ==Background== During the [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|2020 redistricting cycle]], Louisiana's congressional map faced legal challenges for alleged violations of the [[Voting Rights Act of 1965]]. Roughly one-third of Louisiana's population is African American, but only one of Louisiana's six districts was drawn with a Black majority. Legislators overrode Governor [[John Bel Edwards]]' veto to enact the districts. The [[NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund]] sued the state on behalf of Black Louisianan voters. In ''Robinson v. Ardoin'', a [[United States District Court for the Middle District of Louisiana|U.S. District Judge]] found that the maps were illegally racially gerrymandered, first ordering the legislature to reconvene to redraw compliant maps, then suggesting that she would enforce court-ordered maps following legislators' "disingenuous" and "insincere" attempts to do so on their own.{{cite web|last=Muller|first=Wesley|title=Federal court rejects Louisiana congressional map|date=Jun 6, 2022|website=[[States Newsroom|Louisiana Illuminator]]|url=https://lailluminator.com/2022/06/06/federal-court-rejects-louisiana-congressional-map/}}{{cite web|last=Hilburn|first=Greg|title=Judge calls effort of Louisiana Legislature to draw new map 'disingenuous' and 'insincere'|date=Jun 16, 2022|website=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]]|url= https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/news/2022/06/16/federal-judge-calls-louisiana-house-effort-draw-new-map-insincere/7642015001/}} The State appealed the case to the [[United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit|Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals]] to attempt to keep the discriminatory map in place. The Fifth Circuit first placed a stay on the court-ordered redrawing process pending review, then reversed its decision.{{cite web|last=McConnaughey|first=Janet|title=Order for Louisiana to redraw US House districts put on hold|date=Jun 10, 2022|website=[[AP News]]|url=https://apnews.com/article/voting-rights-louisiana-new-orleans-government-and-politics-congress-6a2f606ee9681696387294d40a89afea}}{{cite web|last=McConnaughey|first=Janet|title=Appeals court lifts hold on Louisiana congressional remap|date=Jun 13, 2022|website=[[AP News]]|url=https://apnews.com/article/voting-rights-louisiana-race-and-ethnicity-legislature-969f0d8496439940c766befd3df7e17c}} The State then appealed to the [[Supreme Court of the United States]], which granted the state's application, stayed the district court's injunction, and allowed the [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in Louisiana|2022 elections]] to take place with the discriminatory district map in effect. The Court indicated that it would first review a similar case concerning racial gerrymandering in Alabama, ''[[Allen v. Milligan]]'', before dealing with ''Robinson v. Ardoin.'' The Court was widely expected to side with both Alabama and Louisiana, weakening the anti-discrimination protections of the Voting Rights Act. However, the Court upheld a lower court decision in ''[[Allen v. Milligan]]'' that Alabama's maps were in fact racially gerrymandered, suggesting that it may also decide against Louisiana. On June 26, 2023, the Court decided not to intervene in ''Robinson v. Ardoin'', rescinding its stay and allowing the case to continue in the Fifth Circuit. On November 10, 2023, a decision made by the 5th circuit panel gave the Louisiana state legislature until January 15, 2024, to redraw its congressional maps, with a second majority Black district, in advance of the 2024 election cycle.{{cite web|last1=McGill|first1=Kevin|last2=Sherman|first2=Mark|last3=Cline|first3=Sara|title=Supreme Court unfreezes Louisiana redistricting case that could boost Black voting power before 2024|date=Jun 26, 2023|website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/wireStory/supreme-court-unfreezes-louisiana-redistricting-case-boost-power-100379682}}{{cite web|last=Sneed|first=Tierney|title=Supreme Court allows for Louisiana congressional map to be redrawn to add another majority-Black district|date=Jun 26, 2023|website=[[CNN Politics]]|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/26/politics/supreme-court-louisiana-congressional-redistricting/index.html}}{{Cite web |title=DocumentCloud |url=https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/24160384-robinson-2023-11-10-5th-circuit-opinion |access-date=2023-11-10 |website=www.documentcloud.org}} Because newly elected Governor Jeff Landry was not sworn in until January 8, and a special session of the assembly could not have been convened until at least seven days after the governor calls for one, the Court extended the deadline for the legislature to approve new maps to January 30.{{cite news|last=Mueller|first=Wesley|title=5th Circuit denies Louisiana's appeal in congressional redistricting case|date=Dec 15, 2023|website=Louisiana
